ability.en: skill or talent to do something
ability.ex: She has the ability to learn languages quickly.

about.ex: The trip takes about an hour.

absence.en: lack of something; not being there
absence.ex: The absence of rain hurt the farmers.

example.en: In the absence of clear rules, people did what they liked.
example.zh: 在缺乏明確規則的情況下，人們隨心所欲。

note.usage: 常用 the absence of + 名詞，表示「缺少某物」；in the absence of 意為「在沒有…的情況下」。

noteEn.meaning: the state of something not being there or not existing.
noteEn.usage: Often 'the absence of something' or 'in the absence of something'.

noteEs.exampleTr: A falta de reglas claras, la gente hizo lo que quiso.
noteEs.usage: the absence of + sustantivo = la falta de algo; in the absence of = a falta de.

noteHi.exampleTr: स्पष्ट नियमों के अभाव में लोगों ने जो चाहा वही किया।
noteHi.usage: the absence of + संज्ञा = किसी चीज़ की कमी; in the absence of = के बिना।

noteJa.exampleTr: 明確な規則がなかったので、人々は好きなようにした。
noteJa.usage: the absence of + 名詞で「〜がないこと」。in the absence of は「〜がない場合に」。

noteKo.exampleTr: 명확한 규칙이 없어서 사람들은 원하는 대로 했다.
noteKo.usage: the absence of + 명사: ~의 부족; in the absence of: ~이 없을 때.

acquainted.ex: We became acquainted at a friend's wedding.

activity.en: something people do, often for fun
activity.ex: Swimming is my favourite weekend activity.

affectionately.ex: Locals affectionately call the old dog 'Captain'.
affectionately.ja: 愛情を込めて；親しみを込めて

affiliation.en: official link to a group or religion

example.en: The survey asked about each person's political affiliation.
example.zh: 這份調查詢問了每個人的政治傾向。

note.meaning: （與團體、宗教、政黨的）隸屬或歸屬關係。
note.usage: 常與 religious / political 搭配；affiliation with/to 某團體。

noteEn.meaning: an official connection to a group, religion or political party.
noteEn.usage: Common with 'religious' or 'political'; 'affiliation with' a group.

noteEs.exampleTr: La encuesta preguntaba por la afiliación política de cada persona.
noteEs.meaning: vínculo o pertenencia a un grupo, religión o partido.
noteEs.usage: religious/political affiliation; affiliation with una organización.

noteHi.exampleTr: सर्वेक्षण में हर व्यक्ति की राजनीतिक संबद्धता के बारे में पूछा गया।
noteHi.meaning: किसी समूह, धर्म या दल से संबंध।
noteHi.usage: religious/political affiliation; affiliation with किसी संगठन।

noteJa.exampleTr: その調査では各人の支持政党について尋ねた。
noteJa.meaning: 団体・宗教・政党への所属や結びつき。
noteJa.usage: religious / political affiliation の形が多い。affiliation with 〜で「〜との提携」。

noteKo.exampleTr: 그 설문은 각 사람의 정치적 성향을 물었다.
noteKo.usage: religious / political affiliation 형태가 흔함; affiliation with ~: ~와의 제휴.

affiliation.zh: religious affiliation：宗教歸屬；所屬關係

ago.ex: I moved here ten years ago.

alarmed.ex: Alarmed parents called the school after the storm.

altar.ex: Candles were placed on the altar.
altar.zh: altar boy：祭壇助手（輔祭男孩）

approximately.ex: The film lasts approximately two hours.

as.en: in the role of; when; because

ascended.ex: The hikers ascended the hill before sunrise.

example.en: The balloon began to ascend into the clear sky.
example.zh: 氣球開始升上晴朗的天空。

note.usage: 比 climb / go up 正式；可接受詞 ascend the stairs，亦可指升職 ascend to power。

noteEn.usage: More formal than 'climb'; used with stairs, hills or positions of power.

noteEs.exampleTr: El globo empezó a ascender hacia el cielo despejado.
noteEs.usage: Más formal que climb; ascend the stairs, ascend to power.

noteHi.exampleTr: गुब्बारा साफ़ आसमान में ऊपर उठने लगा।
noteHi.usage: climb से अधिक औपचारिक; ascend the stairs, ascend to power।

noteJa.exampleTr: 気球は澄んだ空へと上昇し始めた。
noteJa.usage: climb より改まった語。ascend the stairs（階段を上る）、ascend to power（権力の座に就く）。

noteKo.usage: climb보다 격식 있는 말; ascend the stairs, ascend to power.

asked.ex: My boss asked me to stay late.

aspires.ex: She aspires to become a doctor.

example.en: Many young players aspire to play for the national team.
example.zh: 許多年輕球員渴望為國家隊效力。

note.usage: 常用 aspire to + 名詞 或 aspire to do，表示懷抱遠大目標。

noteEn.meaning: to strongly hope to achieve something important.
noteEn.usage: Use 'aspire to' + noun or 'aspire to do' something.

noteEs.exampleTr: Muchos jóvenes jugadores aspiran a jugar en la selección nacional.
noteEs.usage: aspire to + sustantivo o aspire to + verbo.

noteHi.exampleTr: कई युवा खिलाड़ी राष्ट्रीय टीम के लिए खेलने की आकांक्षा रखते हैं।
noteHi.meaning: किसी लक्ष्य को पाने की प्रबल इच्छा रखना।
noteHi.usage: aspire to + संज्ञा या aspire to do।

noteJa.exampleTr: 多くの若い選手が代表チームでプレーすることを目指している。
noteJa.meaning: 目標の達成を強く望む。
noteJa.usage: aspire to + 名詞 / aspire to do の形で使う。

noteKo.exampleTr: 많은 젊은 선수들이 국가대표팀에서 뛰기를 열망한다.
noteKo.usage: aspire to + 명사 또는 aspire to do 형태로 씀.

attract.ex: The festival attracts thousands of visitors.

away.ex: Her grandfather passed away last spring.

back.en: the rear part; to an earlier state
back.ex: The garden is at the back of the house.
back.zh: 後面；dating back：追溯至；bring back：恢復

became.ex: He became a teacher at twenty-five.

befriended.ex: She befriended a lonely girl at school.

being.zh: 正在被（被動進行助動詞）

belfry.en: room or tower where bells hang
belfry.ex: Pigeons were nesting in the old belfry.

bell.en: metal object that rings when hit
bell.ex: The school bell rang at noon.

bells.en: metal objects that ring when hit
bells.ex: We heard church bells on Sunday morning.

better.ex: Her temper got the better of her.
better.zh: get the better of：（好奇心）占了上風

boasts.ex: The hotel boasts a huge swimming pool.

boy.ex: The boy kicked the ball over the fence.

brain.en: organ in your head used for thinking
brain.ex: Sleep is important for your brain.

bring.ex: The new mayor wants to bring back the old market.

building.en: a structure with walls and a roof

campanology.en: the art or study of bell ringing
campanology.ex: Campanology needs teamwork and good timing.

cathedrals.ex: Europe has many beautiful old cathedrals.

example.en: The company ceased trading after twenty years.
example.zh: 這家公司在二十年後停止營業。

note.usage: 比 stop 正式；可接 cease + V-ing / to V，或不及物 The noise ceased。

noteEn.usage: A formal word for 'stop'; 'cease to do' or 'cease doing'.

noteEs.exampleTr: La empresa cesó su actividad tras veinte años.
noteEs.usage: Más formal que stop; cease + -ing / to + verbo.

noteHi.exampleTr: कंपनी ने बीस साल बाद कारोबार बंद कर दिया।
noteHi.usage: stop से अधिक औपचारिक; cease to exist, cease operations।

noteJa.exampleTr: その会社は20年後に営業を停止した。
noteJa.usage: stop より改まった語。cease to exist（消滅する）など。

noteKo.usage: stop보다 격식 있는 말; cease to exist, cease operations.

church.ex: They got married in a small church.

churches.ex: The town has three old churches.

city's.ex: The city's parks are very clean.

clean.ex: We clean the kitchen every evening.

cleaned.ex: They cleaned the old garage last weekend.

climbed.ex: We climbed the stairs to the top floor.

cognitive.en: related to thinking and the mind

example.en: Reading every day can slow cognitive decline in older adults.
example.zh: 每天閱讀可以減緩長者的認知退化。

note.meaning: 認知的；與思考、記憶、學習等心智活動有關的。
note.usage: 多用於學術語境，修飾名詞，如 cognitive skills / development / decline。

noteEn.meaning: connected with thinking, remembering and learning.
noteEn.usage: Used before nouns, e.g. 'cognitive skills' or 'cognitive decline'.

noteEs.exampleTr: Leer a diario puede frenar el deterioro cognitivo en los mayores.
noteEs.meaning: relacionado con pensar, recordar y aprender.
noteEs.usage: Palabra académica; cognitive skills, cognitive decline.

noteHi.exampleTr: रोज़ पढ़ने से बुज़ुर्गों में संज्ञानात्मक गिरावट धीमी हो सकती है।
noteHi.meaning: सोचने, याद रखने और सीखने से जुड़ा।
noteHi.usage: अकादमिक शब्द; cognitive skills, cognitive decline।

noteJa.exampleTr: 毎日の読書は高齢者の認知機能の低下を遅らせることがある。
noteJa.meaning: 思考・記憶・学習など心の働きに関する。
noteJa.usage: 学術的な語。cognitive skills、cognitive decline など。

noteKo.exampleTr: 매일 책을 읽으면 노인의 인지 저하를 늦출 수 있다.
noteKo.usage: 학술적인 말; cognitive skills, cognitive decline.

collapse.ex: The old bridge could collapse in a storm.

commonly.ex: This plant is commonly found near rivers.

communal.en: shared by a group of people
communal.ex: The students share a communal kitchen.

community.en: group of people living or acting together
community.ex: The community planted trees in the park.

concerned.ex: Concerned parents met with the head teacher.

consequence.ex: He lost his job as a consequence of the accident.
consequence.zh: as a consequence of：由於…的結果

constructed.ex: The tower was constructed in two years.

cramped.ex: We lived in a cramped flat in the city.

crashing.ex: Waves were crashing against the rocks.

curiosity.en: wish to know or learn something
curiosity.ex: Out of curiosity, she opened the box.

danger.ex: The old house is in danger of falling down.

dating.ex: The castle dates back to the 12th century.

day.ex: One day I will visit Japan.

decades.ex: The tree has grown for decades.

describes.ex: She describes the town as quiet and friendly.

describing.ex: He wrote a letter describing his new home.

direct.ex: She will direct the new school play.

down.ex: He sat down on the bench.

driving.ex: Teamwork was the driving factor in our success.

eclipsing.ex: Her success is eclipsing her brother's.

enlisted.ex: We enlisted friends to help us move.

entice.ex: Free coffee may entice more customers.

escorted.ex: A guard escorted us to the exit.

even.ex: It is even colder today than yesterday.

eventually.en: in the end; after some time
eventually.ex: We eventually found the right road.

exceeding.ex: Speeds exceeding the limit are fined.

faith.ex: Her faith helped her through hard times.

fall.ex: Be careful not to fall on the ice.

fascinated.ex: The children were fascinated by the magic show.

fascination.ex: He has a fascination with old trains.

feared.en: worried that something bad might happen
feared.ex: They feared the river would flood.

fell.ex: The room fell quiet when she spoke.

first.ex: I first met her at university.

flair.ex: She has a flair for languages.

for.en: used to show purpose or time

force.en: a person who makes something happen
force.ex: She was the main force behind the new library.

fr.en: short for Father, a priest's title

gentle.ex: Walking is a gentle way to stay fit.

good.ex: Fresh fruit is good for you.

got.en: (get the better of) became too strong for
got.ex: His anger got the better of him.
got.zh: got the better of：（好奇心）占了上風

group.ex: A group of students visited the museum.

height.ex: The tree grew to a height of ten metres.

held.ex: The school held a concert in May.

helped.ex: My brother helped me paint the room.

higher.ex: The new building is higher than the old one.

hobby.en: an activity you enjoy in free time

hold.ex: Fear began to take hold of the crowd.

hopes.ex: She hopes to visit Japan next year.

hurried.ex: He hurried to catch the bus.

informed.ex: The teacher informed us about the test.

initiative.en: a new plan to solve or improve something
initiative.ex: The town started a new recycling initiative.

example.en: The city launched an initiative to plant more trees.
example.zh: 市政府推動了一項種植更多樹木的計畫。

note.meaning: 為解決問題或改善情況而推動的新計畫、方案。
note.usage: 常與 launch / take 搭配；take the initiative 意為「主動」。

noteEn.meaning: a new plan or project to solve a problem or improve something.
noteEn.usage: Say 'launch an initiative'; 'take the initiative' means act first.

noteEs.exampleTr: La ciudad lanzó una iniciativa para plantar más árboles.
noteEs.meaning: Plan o proyecto nuevo para resolver o mejorar algo.
noteEs.usage: launch an initiative = lanzar una iniciativa; take the initiative = tomar la iniciativa.

noteHi.exampleTr: शहर ने और पेड़ लगाने की एक पहल शुरू की।
noteHi.meaning: किसी समस्या को हल करने या सुधार के लिए शुरू की गई नई योजना।
noteHi.usage: launch an initiative = पहल शुरू करना; take the initiative = खुद पहल करना।

noteJa.exampleTr: 市はもっと木を植える取り組みを始めた。
noteJa.meaning: 問題解決や改善のための新しい計画・取り組み。
noteJa.usage: launch an initiative で「取り組みを始める」、take the initiative で「率先する」。

noteKo.exampleTr: 시는 나무를 더 심는 계획을 시작했다.
noteKo.meaning: 문제를 해결하거나 개선하기 위한 새로운 계획.
noteKo.usage: launch an initiative는 '계획을 시작하다', take the initiative는 '주도하다'.

insists.en: says firmly that something is true
insists.ex: She insists that she locked the door.

interest.en: the feeling of wanting to know more
interest.ex: He has a strong interest in history.

interested.en: wanting to know more about something

invited.ex: They invited me to join the club.

keen.en: wanting very much to do something
keen.ex: She is keen to learn the guitar.

known.ex: The city is known as the Big Apple.

lead.ex: She will lead the team next season.

led.ex: The visitors were led into the hall.

local.ex: We buy bread from a local bakery.

locals.en: people who live in an area
locals.ex: The locals gave us good directions.

loftiest.ex: The loftiest peak was covered in snow.

long-neglected.en: not cared for over a long time

mass.ex: The family went to Mass on Sunday.

met.ex: I met my best friend at school.

mild.ex: Yoga is a mild form of exercise.

mind.en: the part of you that thinks

moderate.en: not too much and not too little
moderate.ex: Moderate exercise is good for the heart.

musical.en: about music or good at music
musical.ex: She comes from a very musical family.
musical.ja: 音楽の；音楽の才能がある

narrow.ex: We walked down a narrow street.

nearby.ex: We ate at a nearby café.

need.ex: You need a ticket to enter.

neglected.ex: The old house was neglected for years.

neither.en: not one and not the other

new.ex: Travel shows you the world in a new way.

newcomers.ex: The club welcomes newcomers every Monday.

normal.ex: The shop is open at normal hours.

not.ex: This soup is not hot enough.

number.ex: A number of students were late today.

observed.ex: From the hill, we observed the whole town.

old.ex: They live in an old house.

once.ex: The sun is once again shining.

originated.ex: The custom originated in ancient China.

note.meaning: 起源於；開始於某時某地。
note.usage: 常用 originate in / from + 地點或時間；為不及物動詞，不用被動。

noteEn.meaning: to begin or come from a certain place or time.
noteEn.usage: Use 'originate in' or 'originate from'; no object needed.

noteEs.exampleTr: La pizza se originó en Italia.
noteEs.meaning: Tener su origen; empezar en un lugar o momento.
noteEs.usage: originate in / from + lugar; verbo intransitivo, sin pasiva.

noteHi.exampleTr: पिज़्ज़ा की शुरुआत इटली में हुई।
noteHi.meaning: किसी स्थान या समय से शुरू होना।
noteHi.usage: originate in / from + स्थान; यह अकर्मक क्रिया है।

noteJa.exampleTr: ピザはイタリアで生まれた。
noteJa.meaning: ある場所や時から始まる、起源を持つ。
noteJa.usage: originate in / from + 場所；自動詞なので受け身にしない。

noteKo.usage: originate in / from + 장소; 자동사라 수동태로 쓰지 않는다.

panoramic.en: showing a wide view of an area
panoramic.ex: The hotel offers panoramic views of the bay.
panoramic.ja: パノラマの；見晴らしの良い

passed.ex: Her grandfather passed away last year.

pastime.en: an activity you do for fun
pastime.ex: Fishing is a popular pastime here.

peals.ex: Peals of bells filled the village square.

people.ex: Many people came to the festival.

period.ex: After a short period of rest, we kept walking.

place.en: (take their place) replace them; (take place) happen
place.ex: The meeting will take place on Friday.

possesses.ex: The museum possesses many rare paintings.

practice.en: doing something again to get better

prerequisite.ex: Patience is a prerequisite for teaching.

example.en: A good night's sleep is a prerequisite for clear thinking.
example.zh: 睡個好覺是頭腦清晰的先決條件。

note.usage: 常用 a prerequisite for / of + 名詞或 V-ing；屬正式用語。

noteEn.meaning: something you must have before you can do something else.
noteEn.usage: Use 'a prerequisite for' something; it is a formal word.

noteEs.exampleTr: Dormir bien es un requisito previo para pensar con claridad.
noteEs.meaning: Condición que se necesita antes de otra cosa.
noteEs.usage: a prerequisite for + sustantivo; palabra formal.

noteHi.exampleTr: स्पष्ट सोच के लिए अच्छी नींद एक पूर्व-शर्त है।
noteHi.meaning: कोई शर्त जो पहले पूरी होनी चाहिए।
noteHi.usage: a prerequisite for + संज्ञा; औपचारिक शब्द।

noteJa.exampleTr: よく眠ることは明晰な思考の前提条件だ。
noteJa.meaning: 事前に必要とされる条件。
noteJa.usage: a prerequisite for 〜 の形で使う。フォーマルな語。

noteKo.usage: a prerequisite for ~ 형태로 쓰며 격식 있는 말이다.

priest.en: a person who leads church services
priest.ex: The priest spoke to the families after Mass.

priests.ex: Two priests work at the cathedral.

prior.en: the head priest of a religious house
prior.ex: The prior welcomed the visitors to the monastery.

project.ex: Our school started a project to plant trees.

provides.ex: The park provides a quiet place to relax.

pursuit.en: an activity you spend time doing
pursuit.ex: Painting is her favourite leisure pursuit.

rear.ex: The exit is at the rear of the bus.

referred.ex: The old man is often referred to as the village wise man.

regular.ex: She makes regular visits to her grandmother.

religion.en: belief in a god or gods
religion.ex: People of every religion are welcome here.

religious.en: believing in and practising a religion
religious.ex: Her family is very religious and prays daily.

replace.ex: We need someone to replace the teacher who left.
replace.ja: 代わりを務める；取り替える

replacements.en: people who take someone else's place
replacements.ex: The team found replacements for the injured players.

required.ex: A passport is required to travel abroad.

residents.en: people who live in a place
residents.ex: Residents complained about the noisy traffic.

restoration.en: repairing something old to its original condition
restoration.ex: The restoration of the old castle took ten years.

example.en: The restoration of the old bridge cost millions.
example.zh: 修復這座舊橋花了數百萬元。

note.meaning: 將老舊或損壞的事物修復回原本的狀態。
note.usage: 常用 the restoration of + 名詞；也可指制度、秩序的恢復。

noteEn.meaning: the work of repairing something old so it is like it was before.
noteEn.usage: Often used as 'the restoration of' + a building or object.

noteEs.exampleTr: La restauración del viejo puente costó millones.
noteEs.meaning: devolver algo viejo o dañado a su estado original.
noteEs.usage: Se usa a menudo como the restoration of + sustantivo.

noteHi.exampleTr: पुराने पुल के जीर्णोद्धार पर लाखों खर्च हुए।
noteHi.meaning: किसी पुरानी या टूटी चीज़ को उसकी मूल स्थिति में लाना।
noteHi.usage: अक्सर the restoration of + संज्ञा के रूप में।

noteJa.exampleTr: 古い橋の修復には何百万もかかった。
noteJa.meaning: 古いものや壊れたものを元の状態に戻すこと。
noteJa.usage: the restoration of 〜 の形でよく使う。

noteKo.exampleTr: 오래된 다리를 복원하는 데 수백만이 들었다.
noteKo.meaning: 낡거나 손상된 것을 원래 상태로 되돌리는 것.
noteKo.usage: 주로 the restoration of + 명사 형태로 쓴다.

restore.en: repair something so it is like new
restore.ex: They plan to restore the old theatre.

return.ex: Fans celebrated the singer's return to the stage.

revival.ex: The town saw a revival of traditional crafts.

ringers.ex: The ringers practise every Thursday evening.

ringing.ex: The phone kept ringing all morning.
ringing.ja: 鳴っている；鳴らすこと

rolled.en: pushed up (sleeves) to start hard work
rolled.ex: He rolled up his sleeves and washed the dishes.
rolled.ja: 腕まくりした（本気で取り組んだ）
rolled.zh: rolled up their sleeves：捲起袖子（開始努力工作）

roof.en: the top covering of a building
roof.ex: Snow covered the roof of the house.

roughly.ex: The trip takes roughly two hours.

routine.ex: The doctor did a routine check-up.

rung.ex: The bell is rung at noon every day.

saw.ex: I saw a rainbow after the storm.

says.ex: My teacher says practice is important.

scaled.en: climbed up something high or steep
scaled.ex: The firefighter scaled the ladder quickly.

seen.ex: I have never seen such a big dog.

served.en: worked or acted in a role
served.ex: She served as class leader for two years.

services.ex: The church holds two services on Sunday.

serving.en: working in a role or duty
serving.ex: He is serving as a volunteer at the hospital.

paragraphs: The bells of a church on Thomas Street in Dublin are ringing again. They were silent for more than 20 years. Local people call the church John's Lane.

Michael Ryan leads a group of bell ringers. More than 50 years ago, he was a boy at this church. One day he climbed the stairs and met the ringers. They took him onto the roof, and he saw Dublin from high up.
About 30 years ago, the bells stopped. Some ringers died, and nobody learned to take their place. This year, the priest Fr Pat Gayer asked Michael to bring the bells back.
The church is about 160 years old. It has the tallest spire in Dublin. Michael hopes more people will try bell ringing. He says it is good for your body and your brain, and you can meet new people.

The bells of a church on Thomas Street in Dublin are ringing again after more than 20 years of silence. The church is St Augustine and St John's, but local people call it John's Lane. A group of bell ringers from other Dublin churches cleaned the old bell tower.

Michael Ryan leads the group. He first became interested in bells more than 50 years ago, when he was an altar boy at the church. One day he climbed the small spiral staircase at the back and met the ringers. They took him onto the roof, and he saw Dublin in a new way.

The bells stopped ringing for normal services about 30 years ago. Some ringers died, and nobody was trained to take their place. This year, the priest Fr Pat Gayer asked Ryan to bring the bells back. When the group practised last week, some neighbours were worried that the bells might fall.

The church was built about 160 years ago and has the tallest spire in Dublin. It is even taller than the city's two cathedrals. Ryan hopes more people will try bell ringing. He says you do not need to be religious or musical. It is a community activity, gentle exercise and good for your brain.

The bells of St Augustine and St John's Church on Thomas Street, Dublin 8, known locally as John's Lane, are ringing for Mass again after more than two decades of silence. Bell ringers from other Dublin church towers helped to clean up the long-neglected belfry.

The project is led by Michael Ryan, who first became fascinated by bell ringing over 50 years ago while serving as an altar boy at the church. He eventually climbed the narrow spiral staircase at the back, met the ringers and was taken onto the roof, where he saw views of the city he had never seen before.

The bells stopped ringing for regular services around 30 years ago, after some ringers died and nobody was trained to replace them. Earlier this year, the church's prior, Fr Pat Gayer, invited Ryan to lead a revival. When the team held practice sessions last week, some alarmed locals told the priests they feared the bells might fall.

Built about 160 years ago, the church has the tallest spire in Dublin, higher than both nearby cathedrals. Ryan now wants more people to take up the hobby. He says religion and musical talent are not required, and describes it as a community activity, mild exercise and good for the brain.

The driving force behind the revival is Michael Ryan, whose fascination with bells took hold over 50 years ago when he was an altar boy at the church. Curiosity eventually got the better of him: he scaled the cramped spiral staircase at the back, befriended the ringers and was led onto the roof, where panoramic views of the city unfolded before him.

The bells fell silent for routine services some three decades ago, as ringers passed away and no successors were trained. Earlier this year, the church's prior, Fr Pat Gayer, enlisted Ryan to spearhead their return. Practice peals last week startled some residents, who hurried into the church to warn the priests that the bells were in danger of crashing down.

Dating back roughly 160 years, the church boasts the loftiest spire in Dublin, eclipsing both neighbouring cathedrals. Ryan is now keen to entice newcomers to the pastime. Neither faith nor musical flair is a prerequisite, he insists, describing campanology as a communal pursuit, a gentle workout and a tonic for the mind.
